initiative.title: In-app image viewer and annotator
initiative.summary: Replace Quick Look with a native in-app image viewer that has RegionShot-grade pan/zoom and RegionShot's basic annotation tools, sharing an annotation model with the session-editing video layer.
initiative.next_action: Start m1: replace .quickLookPreview with overlay ZoomCanvas; run the SwiftUI vs AppKit gesture spike.

sources.anchor: image previews FULLY within the app; cannot open Preview (gross); pan and zoom; basic annotations; whatever RegionShot can do
annotation set: rectangle, arrow, text, highlight, freehand; select/move/resize/delete/undo/redo; RegionShot as reference not component
tools incl. crop; zoom toward pointer, pinch, Cmd +/-/0, trackpad pan, middle-drag pan; single-key tools; handles; linear undo
.quickLookPreview binding used for all mark images
browser pan/zoom lightbox with keys + - 0 1 arrows Esc
exports yes, overlay in the session window

claims.statement: Image viewing happens fully inside the app; Quick Look/Preview are never used.
Pan and zoom with RegionShot-grade handling.
Basic annotations at RegionShot's level: rectangle, arrow, text, highlight, freehand, crop, select/move/resize/delete, undo/redo.
No growth beyond RegionShot's tool set.
Share annotation model and feel with the session-editing video annotation layer.
Original capture is preserved when annotating.
Annotated images appear in Markdown, session.md and Product Grid exports.
Viewer is an overlay inside the session window.

shape.appetite: medium: small viewer, annotation canvas is the bulk; RegionShot basics only
shape.problem: Mark images open in system Quick Look and cannot be inspected or marked up in-app; exports cannot carry annotations.
shape.recommended_shape: Overlay viewer in SessionView replacing .quickLookPreview; shared annotation model (JSON shapes in image pixels) + canvas; flattened PNG cache in annotations/ that process_session.py and PgmExport prefer.

success_moves.move: Ship viewer-only first by replacing the single .quickLookPreview seam; valid state with no annotation code.
Decide SwiftUI vs AppKit NSView canvas from the viewer's gesture feel before building annotation.
Own the annotation model here on stills; video layer in session-editing adds time ranges later.
Non-destructive: JSON + flattened PNG cache; delete annotations/ to roll back.
Export integration is a one-line preference in process_session.py image selection, so Markdown and PgmExport follow automatically.
Flattening/hit-testing are pure functions over the model, unit-testable without UI.

first_proof.question: Can an in-session overlay replace Quick Look with RegionShot-grade pan/zoom, and in SwiftUI or AppKit?
first_proof.artifact: Overlay viewer with pan/zoom from every Quick Look entry point
first_proof.decision_rule: SwiftUI gestures need <=1 workaround -> annotate on same view; else NSView canvas first

rabbit_holes: SwiftUI gesture conflicts (magnify + drag + tool drags)
Text editing inside a zoomed canvas
Card thumbnails stale in ImageCache after save
